review: Reviewed Kai's round-73 request (Evidence-based root cooking: investigate and, if physically feasible, cook two owned raw meadow roots of unknown safety with actually available materials and heat, holding 0.8 branch but no confirmed fire, cookware, water or tools, distinguishing cooking observations from edibility, with real costs and no invented equipment, detoxification, nutrition claims or rewards) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general evidence-based thermal food preparation, not a root-specific interface, to assess or thermally prepare an owned food quantity, inspect work or cancel, with inputStackId, quantity, mode and, for heating, sourceId, support, tool or vessel ids and an evidence reference. Its minimal executable precursor is a paid, evidence-limited feasibility assessment: one active round and 0.2 energy, no food or fuel consumed, the item within actual reach, a report of visible condition, existing treatment records and which supplied prerequisites are unverified or absent, never a claim that no heat source exists anywhere, and failed preconditions spending nothing. Heating needs an actual reachable heat source, a workable exposure and retrieval arrangement and a heating dependency whose round duration, mass and thermal properties, source output, fuel consumption, transfer losses and exposure geometry are coded constants; until that exists heating must report the dependency without charging, and no facility, fire or recipe may be invented. Existing heat representation (search of packages/world-core/src for ignition, combustion, ember, fire and heat). local-fire@1 (forest-fire.ts, forest-fire-environment.ts, forest-fire-exposure.ts) has a built stone hearth, a friction kit, ignition from dry-grass tinder and branch, weather-dependent combustion of fuel lots (at most 1 fuel energy per round, 10% ash, 90% released mass) and warmth for nearby people. It is unscoped, and a development world's registry loads only the foundations and long-ex18 packages, so it cannot be installed here; it needs active-warming@1 and adds thermal-refuge satisfaction triggers, which this incentive scope forbids; and it heats only body temperature, never food. foundation-open@1 probe mode heat needs an object within reach with data.availableHeat > 0 and draws 0.1 from it, and open-processes.ts stations consume availableHeat, but no package ever produces availableHeat and no ex18 object has it. active-warming@1 and forest-thermal.ts concern body temperature only; food-water.ts uses air temperature for evaporation. Resources carry a hidden fuel value (branch 8, bark 5, dry grass 4), but no food has heat capacity, temperature, cooking or scorching thresholds, and no rule maps heat to a food hazard. The ex18 world at round 73 holds only foundation-forest, foundation-open, foundation-expression, plant-establishment-trial and unheated-food-preparation, with no hearth, fire or heat source. Heating therefore cannot be grounded in the existing world rules: its required heat-transfer parameters would have to be invented, which the specification itself and this handoff exclude. Following the specification's own fallback, implemented thermal-food-preparation@1 (scope long-ex18, handler long.thermal-food-preparation, equivalence food:thermal-preparation:assess-heat:1, learning 3; references inputStackId 'optional-exact-visible'; the ability serializes to 2,534 code units, within the 3,500 limit; visualComponents [] because no object is created; its one event, thermal-feasibility-assessed, is the declared practice evidence and never carries a qualified flag). Modes: assess and heat. Assess: inputStackId is the exact id of the person's own unreserved stack that passes the eat edibility test; quantity (exact tenths, default the whole stack) must not exceed it; optional sourceId, up to four apparatusIds and evidenceKey, each id at most once and different from the food. Every check, including energy of at least 0.2, runs before the charge. It costs one round and 0.2 energy, consumes, moves, reserves and heats nothing, and writes an unverified personal record (key <item>:thermal-feasibility) and the event, both carrying an assessment id, input, considered quantity, position and tick; the food's look (quantity, origin, harvest round, decay, condition, visible spoilage, treatment records, safety unknown) with heated false, cooked false and edibility 'not established'; the person's own eating record of that food, labelled as not a test of the stack; the proposed source as absent, present without represented heat, or present with represented heat; every object within interaction reach with represented heat; each apparatus id as absent or present with an unverified role; local water; the evidence key as present (subject, property, verified flag) or absent; processingRule null; missing prerequisite codes (heat-source unless a represented source is present, exposure-support unless a supplied support is present, and always heat-transfer); the unverified and absent id lists; heating {available false, dependency, reason}; and display metadata (food raw-unchanged, heating dependency-blocked, indicator missing-prerequisites) for a later drawing, with no cooked or success state. Heat: refused before any cost with the message that this world represents no usable heat source, no heat transfer into food and no food thermal properties; the kernel records it as an observable failed event and nothing is spent, even when a represented heat source is within reach. Inspect-work and cancel are not included: heating work can never start, so there is nothing to inspect, pause, resume or cancel; they belong to the future heating dependency. Modeling assumptions. (1) Owned stacks are carried: eat, give and drop act on them anywhere and observation reports them at the carrier, so the selected food is within reach and a stale recorded position (such as Kai's branch at (11.4, 18.25)) does not matter. Ground items count within pickup reach (radius plus 0.65) and objects within interaction reach; other people's items and anything farther are reported absent, and nothing hidden is searched or revealed. (2) A represented heat source is exactly the probe's heat rule, an object within reach with available heat; items, including branches, are never heat sources, so a branch is reported present without represented heat, never as fuel or ignition. (3) Ignition is reported as not assessed because it depends on the actual source. (4) No heating method is defined, so no item or object can be confirmed as a support, tool, vessel or water supply; supplied ones are present with an unverified role, and exposure-support is missing only if none is present. (5) Local water is the probe's wetting rule: water terrain in the person's own cell. (6) No processing rule maps heat to any food hazard, so an evidence key is only checked for existence and the assessment never labels food edible, cooked or safe; existing treatment records such as dry brushing are listed and never treated as heating. (7) A repeated assessment overwrites the same personal record and costs again. (8) Incentives are on and only the existing experience implementation applies: no satisfaction source, reward, mood or account write is added; the record is unverified, so no information-confirmed event follows; the event has no qualified flag, so the automatic practice rule never fires on an assessment or a missing-prerequisite list; no object is made, so work-noticed is unaffected; physical wellbeing changes only through the spent energy. Reuse: long-unheated-food-preparation.ts look and owned (only exported; that package serializes byte-identically, its SHA-256 is pinned in the new test, and its test file passes unchanged) and its eating-record report; open-foundation.ts openRemember with the probe's observation cost, heat rule and wetting rule; collective-food-profile.ts; forest-food-accounting.ts; continuous-geometry.ts. ex15 food-preparation@1 and E1 controlled-food-processing-trial@1 are not reused because their texts, recipes and costs differ, and local-fire@1 is not reused for the reasons above; every earlier package is unchanged. This is a simplified real mechanism for the specification's executable precursor (a real cost, a real personal record and an observable event), not a first release that spends nothing; the thermal mode is a documented, dependency-blocked part rejected before costs because the world cannot represent a heat source or heat transfer into food. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex18-thermal-food-preparation.test.ts, built with initialLongWorld('long-ex18', 'the incentive-control scenario') and two roots actually gathered from commons-root-1-0) cover scope, unique handlers, the text limit, excluded vocabulary, the byte-identical reused package and three-round study; the one-round 0.2-energy cost; conservation of every stack and its ageing; the record and event; supplied present, unverified and absent references and a branch as no heat source; treatment records; the probe heat rule with heating still refused; refusals of heating and invalid assessments without spending, with the observable failed event; owner-only assessment and personal records; and no reward under the existing incentives.
